newsitem.title: USA: InterCel postpones debt deal, says no PCS delays.
newsitem.headline: InterCel postpones debt deal, says no PCS delays.

text.p: InterCel Inc on Friday said deteriorating market conditions prompted it to postpone its planned $300 million debt offering.

Allen Smith, chief executive officer and president, said cash reserves of more than $200 million will allow the company to proceed with its personal communication service build out in Atlanta and then Tennessee and Kentucky markets without an immediate access of the capital markets.
"I don't have to go out right now in this kind of market climate and expose my shareholders to the kind of pricing that is there now," Smith said.
The deal was to begin an investor roadshow today.

Proceeds from the deal were slated to fund build out of InterCel's Powertel PCS in 13 Basic Trading Areas in Kentucky and Tennessee, Smith said. Plans for a fourth quarter 1998 deployment of Powertel are not affected by the decision to temporarily abandon the capital markets, he added.

"We've got 16 markets operational, we're building Atlanta that is well on schedule, and from a timing standpoint and the cash position were in its not incumbent to come to market and accept an interest rate we don't think is commensurate with the quality of the company, the CEO said.
Smith said it was too soon to tell when the company would access the debt market. The company may make a decision until after the meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee next Tuesday, he said.
InterCel was the winning bidder of 13 Basic Trading Areas in January 1997, which give the company a contiguous footprint 12 Southeastern states. Licenses were paid for with equity, the CEO said.

The planned debt offering was rated B2 by Moody's Investors Service and single-B by Standard & Poor's. S&P on March 19 also upgraded the ratings of InterCel's corporate credit and outstanding debt to single-B from single-B-minus.
The company is based in West Point, Georgia.
